p: Pattern: an extreme close-up of a soft, fine-textured warm surface filling the crop, centred just beside a dark rounded blob, with small dark ovals nearby and a sharp edge on one side. Examples: the cheek, muzzle side or eye area of a long-furred dog seen very close.
k305: Pattern: a large rounded snout or dark blob so close that it fills much of the crop and no outline fits, often with an open mouth below it. Examples: dogs' noses and muzzles seen very near, a bird's eye up close, bare skin close up.
k97: Pattern: hard, smooth or glossy surfaces with crisp edges, printing or bands, and no soft texture. Examples: bottles, mugs and jars, printed labels and text, metal parts, a plane's wing, rows of matchsticks.
k23: Pattern: dense, busy, high-contrast repeated texture covering the whole crop: many small similar cells, dots, spots or stripes in a regular tiling, with no single central shape. Examples: butterfly wings, keyboards, patterned fabric, spotted fur, lattices.
k297: Pattern: an upright shape: a rounded top patch over a wide flat solid-coloured block filling the lower half. Examples: a person's chin, neck and shirt or jacket front, the chest of an animal seen from the front.
k163: Pattern: a dark rounded mass at the centre with a pale vertical stripe running down its middle, flanked by two dark patches. Examples: a dog's face seen head-on with a white blaze between dark eyes, a skunk's face, a dark round object with a bright highlight stripe.
k275: Pattern: a round dark disc with concentric rims at the centre, a small bright glint, no lines radiating from it. Examples: an animal's eye with iris and pupil seen very close, a round lens, a dark round hole or filter.
c101: Pattern: a flat area with no central structure: smooth warm reddish or brown surfaces, straight edges or horizontal bands, no ring of fibres and no hub. Examples: wood, cloth, painted walls, furniture, a warm-coloured horizontal patch.
